subject: math

objective.text: Round numbers to any place using a vertical number line. Estimate sums and differences.

explanations.title: Round to the nearest ten thousand
explanations.text: Find the ten thousand below and the ten thousand above. The halfway point is 5 thousands more than the lower one.

explanations.title: Round to the nearest hundred thousand
explanations.text: Find the hundred thousand below and above. The halfway point is 5 ten thousands more than the lower one.

explanations.title: Nearer endpoint
explanations.text: Mark the number on the line. It rounds to the endpoint it is nearer to. At the halfway point, round up.

explanations.title: Estimate a sum
explanations.text: Round each addend to the same place. Then add the rounded numbers.

explanations.title: Estimate a difference
explanations.text: Round each number to the same place. Then subtract. Rounding to a smaller unit gives an estimate closer to the actual answer.

examples.title: Round 72,744 to the nearest ten thousand
examples.text: 72,744 is between 70,000 and 80,000. The halfway point is 75,000. 72,744 is nearer to 70,000, so it rounds to 70,000.

examples.title: Round 749,085 to the nearest hundred thousand
examples.text: 749,085 is between 700,000 and 800,000. The halfway point is 750,000. It rounds to 700,000.

examples.title: Estimate 505,341 plus 193,841
examples.text: Round to the nearest hundred thousand: 500,000 plus 200,000 is 700,000.

examples.title: Estimate 35,555 minus 26,555
examples.text: Nearest ten thousand: 40,000 minus 30,000 is 10,000. Nearest thousand: 36,000 minus 27,000 is 9,000.

hints.text: Find the number halfway between the two numbers. Think about which unit is different.
Split the number at the unit. Count the units on the left and the rest on the right.
Round each cost to the nearest thousand. Then add the rounded costs.
Say how many of the unit are in the number.
The halfway point is half of one unit above the lower endpoint.
Find the endpoint below and above. Compare with the halfway point.
Round each number to the same place first. Then add or subtract.
Think of the least and the greatest numbers that round to the given number.
Think about how many numbers changed when you rounded.

The number of units shown beside each endpoint

assets_required.interaction: Child picks a place and enters a number. The line shows endpoints and midpoint and marks the number. The child picks the nearer endpoint.
